title: Mesh Invaiant Infinite Dimensional Adaptive MCMC for Latent Gaussian Processes
topic: Probabilistic Methods->Monte Carlo and Sampling Methods
claim: Restricting adaptation to a truncated subspace changes learned scales and step-size convergence, with full-space variants adapting poorly and slowly.
layout: 3 line-plot panels in a row, shared legends in lower right
description: Three side-by-side line plots, each with a legend at lower right. Left: variance multiplier d against KL coordinate index (0 to 400). A black oracle curve and a smooth green truncated pCN_MV estimate both rise from 0 to about 1 and stay there. A noisy red global variant oscillates between about 0.8 and 1.3 around that level. Middle: adaptation of beta over 100k iterations. The green truncated curve climbs quickly to 1.0 by about 30k iterations. The red global variant drops to about 0.15 and then drifts up to about 0.35. Right: beta against iteration for pCNL variants, over 55k iterations. Purple, magenta and blue/orange curves rise to 1 at different speeds, a light-blue line stays flat at 1, and a gray line stays near 0. The eye goes to the contrast between the green and red curves.
caption: Effect of truncating the online adaptation. Left: estimates of the variance multipliers dk in KL coordinates for the truncated pCNMV updates, and the oracle values d⋆,k. Middle: adaptation of β for pCNMV variants under target acceptance 0.234. Right: adaptation of β for pCNLV variants under target acceptance 0.53.
abstract: We introduce mesh-invariant adaptive Markov chain Monte Carlo methods for Gaussian-process posteriors arising in infinite-dimensional Bayesian inference. In function-space MCMC, posterior distributions are defined by a change of measure with respect to a Gaussian prior, making absolute continuity essential for valid proposal construction. Standard adaptive schemes that modify means or scales in the full discretized space can destroy this property, leading to proposal measures that become singular in the infinite-dimensional limit. To avoid this, we adapt only an active finite-dimensional subspace of the Gaussian-process representation while preserving the prior dynamics on inactive coordinates. This yields two adaptive proposals, pCNLV and pCNMV, which extend preconditioned Crank--Nicolson and Crank--Nicolson Langevin methods by learning posterior scale, and in pCNMV also posterior mean structure, on the data-informed subspace without introducing discretization-dependent Gaussian density ratios. The resulting samplers retain the mesh robustness of function-space methods while improving efficiency through local adaptation. Experiments on a Darcy-flow inverse problem and Bayesian logistic regression demonstrate consistent efficiency gains, including an approximately fourfold improvement in effective sampling efficiency for Darcy flow.
